title: if-else Conditionals
concept: A basic branching statement that executes different code depending on conditions

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation:
**`int main() {`** -- The entry point of the program. When `main` is called, a **stack frame** is created on the stack.

In this lesson, we use a single `temperature` variable to learn how to **branch program flow based on conditions**.

steps.title: Initializing the temperature variable
steps.explanation: **`int temperature = 35;`** -- Declares an integer variable `temperature` and initializes it to **35**. In this single line, 4 bytes of space are allocated within the stack frame, and `35` is stored in that space.

steps.title: Evaluating the if condition (true)
steps.explanation: **`if (temperature >= 30) {`** -- Here comes the core of this lesson: the **if statement**. If the condition inside the parentheses is **true (a non-zero value)**, the code inside the curly braces executes; if it is **false (0)**, it is skipped.

steps.title: Executing the true branch (output)
steps.explanation:
**`printf("It's hot!\n");`** -- Since the condition was true, this line executes and `It's hot!` is printed to the screen.

The most important rule of an if-else if-else chain is that once a condition is true, only that block executes and all remaining `else if` and `else` blocks are **entirely skipped**.

steps.title: Skipping else if / else
steps.explanation: **`} else if (temperature >= 20) {`** -- Since the preceding `if` condition was already true, this `else if` and the `else` block below are **skipped entirely without even being evaluated**. The expression `temperature >= 20` is never executed.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation: **`return 0;`** -- After the conditional branching is done, the program terminates normally. `return 0` signals to the operating system that "everything ended without problems", and as main's stack frame is deallocated, `temperature` disappears from memory.

quiz.explanation:
An if-else if chain checks conditions from top to bottom and executes only the block of the first condition that is true.
When temperature = 20, the first condition (>= 30) is false, and the second (>= 20) is true, so only B is printed.
The third (>= 10) is also true, but since the second already matched, it is never executed.

misconceptions.wrong: else if conditions are always checked
misconceptions.correct: If any preceding if or else if is true, all subsequent else if / else blocks are skipped.
misconceptions.why: if-else if-else forms a 'chain', so once the first true block is found, the rest are ignored.

keyTakeaway: An if-else if-else chain checks conditions from top to bottom and executes only the first block whose condition is true.
